newsitem.title: USA: U.S. calls on Serbia to heed Gonzalez report.
newsitem.headline: U.S. calls on Serbia to heed Gonzalez report.

text.p: The United States on Friday welcomed international confirmation of opposition victories over Serbia's ruling Socialist party in local elections last month and called on Belgrade to accept the results.

"The U.S. applauds the work" of former Spanish Prime Minister Felipe Gonzalez, whose Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe fact-finding panel on Friday backed opposition claims that the authorities had cheated them out of election victories, the State Department said.
It said Gonzalez' conclusions "match our own" and Serbia "must honour international commitments and move toward democracy before it can be accepted fully into the international community."

Serbian courts, at what Western countries said was the instigation of President Slobodan Milosevic, had overturned the results of the Nov. 17 elections. Gonzalez told a news conference in Geneva Serbian authorities should accept opposition victories in 22 disputed municipalities, including the nine in Belgrade.

State Department spokesman John Dinger told reporters: "We call on President Milosevic to heed the recommendations of the Gonzalez report and we point out that President Milosevic did agree to the visit by the OSCE delegation."

He added: "We believe that the best way possible to resolve this situation is for President Milosevic to now heed the delegation's recommendations ... that he respect the results of the Nov. 17 elections, that he engage in an open and constructive dialogue with the opposition and that Serbia honour its international commitments to move toward democracy."
In Belgrade, a crowd of some 80,000 danced and cheered at news of Gonzalez' report, but opposition leaders were sceptical that Milosevic would respond positively to it.
